Build a surface from a precomputed grid

Source: R/surf-grid.R
surf_grid.Rd

Wraps a cross-validated loss over two tuning axes, or any other grid of values computed outside a fitted model, as an effectsurf object so that plot.effectsurf(), surf_contour(), surf_optimum() and surf_export() work on it. The surface is typed as a score, and print output and default captions report it as a cross-validated score.

Usage

surf_grid(
  data,
  x,
  y,
  z,
  conf_low = NULL,
  conf_high = NULL,
  direction = c("maximise", "minimise"),
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

data

A data.frame with one row per grid cell.

x

Character. Name of the column holding the first tuning axis.

y

Character. Name of the column holding the second tuning axis.

z

Character. Name of the column holding the score at each cell.

conf_low, conf_high

Character or NULL. Names of columns holding a lower and upper band around the score; the mean minus and plus one standard error draws the band the one-standard-error rule reads. Both or neither must be given.

direction

Character. "maximise" when a larger score is better, "minimise" when a smaller score is better (a loss).

labels

A named list with display labels: x, y, z, title. Any element not given is built from the column names.

Value

An object of class effectsurf with type = "score", whose z_var is the original name of the z column.

Details

The grid must be rectangular: every combination of the distinct x and y values present in data appears exactly once. A grid over the number of variables admitted is ragged at the ends where one tuning value admits more variables than another, and the error names each missing cell so the grid can be restricted to the range every y value reaches.

direction records whether larger or smaller values are better. It is stored in meta$direction and read by surf_optimum() when type is not given, so the optimum of a loss surface is its minimum without further instruction.

See also

new_effectsurf() for the low-level constructor, surf_optimum() for the optimum.

Author

Max Moldovan, max.moldovan@adelaide.edu.au

Examples

cv <- expand.grid(n_selected = 1:8, alpha = c(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 1))
cv$loss <- (cv$n_selected - 5)^2 + (cv$alpha - 0.6)^2
es <- surf_grid(cv, x = "n_selected", y = "alpha", z = "loss",
                direction = "minimise")
print(es)
#> ℹ <effectsurf> — Cross-Validated Score Surface
#> • X: n_selected | Y: alpha | Z: loss
#> • Grid: 40 points (40 per stratum)
#> • CI: FALSE | Transform: FALSE
#> • Score computed outside a model; smaller is better
#> ℹ Use `plot()` to visualise, `surf_data()` to extract data.
surf_optimum(es)
#> ℹ Surface min found:
#> • n_selected = 5
#> • alpha = 0.6
#> • estimate = 0
#>    n_selected alpha estimate
#>         <int> <num>    <num>
#> 1:          5   0.6        0
